TRAVELUTION TRAVEL SCAM

By: Latashia Naidoo | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As the world reopens for travel, we investigate a travel scam that’s left hundreds of locals out of pocket.

Unique Selling Point:
Travel scams are in the spotlight, with swindlers promising travellers the world but instead taking them for a ride to nowhere.

Summary:
The adage: “If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is” certainly rang true for scores of would-be holidaymakers, who claim they’ve been conned by leisure travel company, MyTravelution.

The members-only lifestyle travel club offers users exclusive packages at unbeatable prices - on a monthly payment and commission-structured basis.
But after being invited to presentations in which they were promised dream vacations for a monthly fee, clients said it sounded too good to be true - because it was.
They allege that debit orders were 2 to 3 times more than what they’d initially signed up for, that refunds promised during the initial cooling period have not been returned - years later; that documents they never signed were forged, and that the company also demands a R24 000 cancellation fee - even if/when the services have not been used.

More than 60 criminal cases have since been lodged against the company since 2014, with disgruntled clients claiming they have very little hopes of ever getting their monies back.
Some people, like Tazkia Abrahams, invested R400 000 into the company.
She is also a former employee of MyTravelution, and wants to expose the company’s fraudulent activities.
Lutfiya Alli’s honeymoon plans were ruined after she paid R100k to the company - for a trip that never got off the ground.
While Cindy van Wyk has been trying for years to recover tens of thousands of rands from the company - to no avail.
Paul Anderson and his fiancé invested R15 000 into a travel package, and when they demanded a refund - were told they’re number 171 on the company’s refund list.
These are just some of scores of angry clients who want their monies back, and for justice to be served.

A possible confront with the CEO of MyTravelution, to find out where clients monies have been funnelled to - when no travel has taken place.

Further information:
The Association of Southern African Travel Agents (Asata) has also warned potential holidaymakers to be aware of the rise in travel scams they’ve been alerted to of late.
The body said it is regularly contacted by consumers whose holiday plans have gone awry because they booked a holiday package that was “too good to be true”, they were scammed or defrauded by a travel provider - and have to now live with the financial fallouts of their ‘dream’ holidays turning into a walking nightmare.

MyTravelution - Final:

VO:
It’s a weeknight in Bellville, Cape Town. The sales division of a travel agency called MyTravelution seems to be doing a brisk trade as prospective clients attend a pitch meeting…

VO:
In the crowd, our producer with a hidden camera.

SALESPERSON:
“We’ve got nothing to do with points, we’ve got nothing to do with timeshare. What we do is very straightforward, okay. We’re a travel agency. The only difference is that we are the wholesaler in the travel industry.”

VO:
The promise of 5 star holidays in exotic destinations…
and the opportunity to travel the world - on a budget.

Cindy:
“We were offered a 40% discount on flights, accommodation, and car hire…”

VO:
All potential clients had to do was attend a presentation, sign up, and experience all the unbelievable benefits for themselves.

Cindy
“It was a very upbeat presentation, where they offered a lot of discounts…”

VO:
But that travel bubble soon burst…

LINK
Over the years, Carte Blanche has been inundated with complaints about the MyTravelution travel scheme - where clients are promised “a whole new world of vacation possibilities” - at a fraction of luxury travel costs. But for many disgruntled clients etc [Masa goes on]

VO:
Dozens of disgruntled clients belonging to the MyTravelution travel scheme are now accusing the company of taking them on a financial ride…

VO:
They say MyTravelution has failed to make their dream vacation plans take flight…

VO:
Members allege that the ritzy advertising seemed misleading...the huge savings offers altogether false.. the contracts - deceptive... and the hidden costs VERY high.

CINDY:
“All I was thinking of was this 40% I can save on flights; I get a free holiday as well for joining, I pay R25000 once off and R436 for 24 months - that’s it, and I get these discounts forever.”

VO:
Luckily, Cindy van Wyk is an avid and streetwise traveller... MyTravelution’s promises of massive savings would have been fantastic for her - but she realised there was no such a thing as a free holiday.

VO:
She alleges MyTravelution consultants forged her signature on a contract she never signed.

Masa:
“The very next day after the presentation, you get a contract with your signature on it that you didn’t sign - that goes completely against everything they promised you in the presentation?”

CINDY:
“The very next day, not even 24 hours later, I get a signed contract. This contract was never explained to us in the presentation, they never presented us with this contract in the presentation….”

VO:
But that wasn’t all.
Remember all those promised savings? In Cindy’s contract, those were conspicuously missing.

“And to top it all off, when we read the contract, it specifically says there’s no discounts for flights, for car hire, or hotels.”

——-

VO:
We set out to investigate this travel club - which has earned a bit of a reputation for being a scam - promising benefits they can’t deliver.

VO:

MyTravelution was the brainchild of managing director Thilo Lippert and sales director Craig Browne.

VO:
It’s one of at least five travel companies they own and operate.

VO:

MyTravelution offers travel packages and another company of theirs called the Nexus Group markets the deals in a multi-level marketing scheme - a controversial network marketing structure where members promote the company and earn its income…

VIZ: Hidden camera footage of the presentations

Remember that presentation we attended?

Well, after potential members are told about the amazing savings they can get just by joining MyTravelution… there’s the harder sell:

VIZ: flipping through Nexus brochure

.. the option to earn referral-based commissions through the Nexus Affiliate Partnership programme - but only if two referrals join myTravelution and pay the full activation fee - between R1 and R40 000.

VIZ: Graphic of pyramid scheme

Here’s how Sales Director, Craig Browne explains their sales drive…

Craig:
“… since we launched the 30 000 job-creating challenge here in South Africa with the Nexus Group, we have been able to get invites to over 5000 people. Over a thousand of those have taken up the offer, taken up the challenge and decided to join the cause.”

Both Craig and Thilo Lippert use the company’s social media pages almost like a personal vlog -

Thilo:
“The Nexus Group, “live life checking in”, let’s start her up.”

… to spread the gospel of their company's offerings, and wax lyrical about their successes.

VIZ; CRAIG 4
Craig: “the new Nexerians that have signed up. You know, we are so grateful - the original Nexus Group core - we are so grateful for every single new Nexerian that has come in the door and joined the cause…”

But… none of these videos address members’ complaints.

VO:
Hundreds of former clients are currently owed millions in refunds for contract cancellations and commissions -

Some have been waiting for months; others - years.

VO:
Everyone we spoke to claimed the company refused to refund their activation fees - even though they cancelled within the five day cooling off period.

VO:
The Consumer Protection Act says people should be able to get refunds when they change their minds - about ANY deal.

TRUDIE:
“They don’t acknowledge an email cancellation. They don’t even acknowledge a cancellation that’s been done by courier.”

VO:
Not illegal. But not kosher business practice, either.

VO:
It’s HOW the company has allegedly attempted to swindle members out of their cash - with large sign-up costs, and hidden fees when they take up the travel offers.

VO:
Consumer lawyer Trudie Broekmann has spent five years challenging the company’s business practices.


TRUDIE:
“The marketing is substantially misleading, deceptive, fraudulent, false. The service offering really is practically speaking non-existent.”…

VO:
Trudie represents 58 clients who are seeking refunds from the company.


Masa: “Would you call this a scam?”

Trudie:
“Lawyers don’t really use that word… I would say that this is a business which operates in a substantially misleading and deceptive manner, and a deceptive manner. Their contracts don’t comply with the Consumer Protection Act, and these aren’t a few small non-compliances. No, there are dramatic divergences from what the law requires of contract.”

VO:
Those divergences include various contraventions of the Consumer Protection Act - such as:

Failing to waive the client’s right to cancel their contract,
And providing misleading offers and information.

——-
VO:

With MyTravelution and the Nexus Group, more than 50 people flooded our inbox with their stories.

And through months of investigations, we found some patterns…

VO:
Allegations of misappropriation of members’ funds…
failure to pay commissions…
And… travel deals which never manifest.

CINDY:
“All I can say is: if it sounds too good to be true, don’t go for it. Nothing is cheap anymore, nothing is free anymore.”

VO:
We put these allegations to the directors and their legal representative - who claimed we had no basis for our investigations.

VO:
They chose not to respond.

VO:
So we went in search of answers - firsthand.

MASA LINK:
Behind me is one of the Nexus Group’s sales offices. It’s here where potential clients are enticed with glamorous sales pitches offering 5 star luxury holidays and massive discounts on flights and travel.
But, all is not what it seems.

Hidden Footage:
Marc: “This is for two flights, two x meals, 2 x transfers and airport taxes, all non-alcoholic beverages, your package lasts for one week free. You’re gonna pay this for two people.”
Tash: “8204 - for two people?”
Marc: “This is what you’re getting free - accommodation and everything free.”

VO:
The MyTravelution contract specifies that clients will not receive discounts on flights…

VO:
… Yet in the marketing pitch there were huge savings on air tickets - and even on business class travel.

——

VO:
While everyone we spoke to alleged the same thing…

“I really do believe that they are scamming people, and committing fraud…”

“They are fraudsters.”

“… unscrupulous behaviour.”

“It’s a scam, stay away.”


VO:

VO:
More than sixty x 1-star reviews on HelloPeter speak of general member unhappiness.

TASH: “We were hesitant about coming here because there were a few that called it a ‘scam’.”

Johan: “Can I shock you quickly? 90% of those people who said it’s a scam - the few there - are not even members.”


VO:
But former employees claimed that Nexus Group employees were told to create pseudo accounts and post fake positive reviews on the site - to counter all the negatives.

VO:
We decided to set the record straight - in person…

CONFRONT:
Masa looking in
Cut to 01:44
“Do you work here? Hi, I’m from Carte Blanche…”

Masa PTC: “So we came to try to offer MyTravelution’s directors a right of reply - they have already declined… but we really wanted to know their side of the story.”

VO:
And that’s when security showed up…

We were told that the directors weren’t on premises
So we left… with more unanswered questions.
——

VO:
When it comes to the issue of refunds, the company is pleading poverty.

——-

VO:
… It’s just one of the reasons that the consumer watchdog - the National Consumer Commission - is investigating MyTravelution specifically - for alleged fraudulent misrepresentation, non-compliance, and contravention of consumer law.

VO:
Prudence Moilwa is Head of Enforcement and Investigations at the NCC.

PRUDENCE:
“What we pick up is that they sell themselves as a company that provides cheaper travel options for their members. But when you look at their contract, it seems to be contrary to exactly what they market themselves to be.”

VO:
If found guilty of these infringements, MyTravelution could face a fine of
R1 million, or 10% of their annual turnover.

——-

VO:
Meanwhile, MyTravelution’s unhappy clients are hoping that the next trip the company’s directors take is to court, for what they allege is criminal conduct.


TRUDIE:
“… It feels as though it’s a failure of the legal system to date. Part of it is that the wheels turn so incredibly slow, because we’ve been waiting for their day of reckoning to arrive.”


——-

PROMOS:

PROMO:
If the promise of a free luxury holiday with no hidden costs sounds too good to be true, that’s probably because it is!
But how can you tell if something is legit - or if you’re about to be taken for the financial ride of your life?

Trudie:
“There’s no such thing as a free lunch, right? So there’s also no such thing as a free holiday in the Maldives or Mauritius.”

——

PROMO:
As the world reopens for international travel, we investigate a travel company that’s left dozens of clients with their dream travel plans - grounded.

Trudie:
“The marketing is substantially misleading, deceptive, fraudulent, false. The service offering really is practically non-existent.”…

——

PROMO:
They were promised the world… or at least the opportunity to travel it.
But dozens of would-be travellers claim they’ve been taken for a financial ride by an unscrupulous travel company

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): As the world reopens for travel, we investigate a travel scam that’s left hundreds of locals out of pocket.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Travel scams are in the spotlight, with swindlers promising travellers the world but instead taking them for a ride to nowhere.
metadata.Summary: The adage: “If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is” certainly rang true for scores of would-be holidaymakers, who claim they’ve been conned by leisure travel company, MyTravelution. The members-only lifestyle travel club offers users exclusive packages at unbeatable prices - on a monthly payment and commission-structured basis. But after being invited to presentations in which they were promised dream vacations for a monthly fee, clients said it sounded too good to be true - because it was. They allege that debit orders were 2 to 3 times more than what they’d initially signed up for, that refunds promised during the initial cooling period have not been returned - years later; that documents they never signed were forged, and that the company also demands a R24 000 cancellation fee - even if/when the services have not been used. More than 60 criminal cases have since been lodged against the company since 2014, with disgruntled clients claiming they have very little hopes of ever getting their monies back. Some people, like Tazkia Abrahams, invested R400 000 into the company. She is also a former employee of MyTravelution, and wants to expose the company’s fraudulent activities. Lutfiya Alli’s honeymoon plans were ruined after she paid R100k to the company - for a trip that never got off the ground. While Cindy van Wyk has been trying for years to recover tens of thousands of rands from the company - to no avail. Paul Anderson and his fiancé invested R15 000 into a travel package, and when they demanded a refund - were told they’re number 171 on the company’s refund list. These are just some of scores of angry clients who want their monies back, and for justice to be served. A possible confront with the CEO of MyTravelution, to find out where clients monies have been funnelled to - when no travel has taken place.
metadata.Further information: The Association of Southern African Travel Agents (Asata) has also warned potential holidaymakers to be aware of the rise in travel scams they’ve been alerted to of late. The body said it is regularly contacted by consumers whose holiday plans have gone awry because they booked a holiday package that was “too good to be true”, they were scammed or defrauded by a travel provider - and have to now live with the financial fallouts of their ‘dream’ holidays turning into a walking nightmare.
